title: Nvidia Moves On From Jensen Huang

summary.headline: Nvidia beats earnings expectations; Trump meets Xi and Putin on nuclear arms
summary.tldr: Nvidia reported strong financial results and raised guidance despite a leadership change, signaling robust demand for AI chips. Meanwhile, President Trump is in China for a trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin to discuss nuclear arms control.

key_points.point: Nvidia reported $115 billion in quarterly revenue, exceeding analyst expectations of 109 billion.
key_points.why_it_matters: Strong performance suggests the company's AI-driven growth remains resilient even during a transition away from founder Jensen Huang.

key_points.point: Nvidia plans to stop selling hopper chips into China, citing a focus on high-demand markets elsewhere.
key_points.why_it_matters: This marks a significant shift in strategy, moving away from the previous argument that selling to China maintained US technological leverage.

key_points.point: President Trump is meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin to discuss a potential three-way nuclear arms control agreement.
key_points.why_it_matters: The meeting highlights China's growing nuclear arsenal and its desire to be recognized as a peer power on the global stage.

key_points.point: Democrats flipped a Senate seat in Alaska, expanding their incoming majority to 56 seats.
key_points.why_it_matters: This result represents the largest number of Senate seats flipped by Democrats since 1958, impacting the legislative landscape.

key_points.point: Waymo suspended robotaxi operations on US freeways following a California state ban after safety incidents.
key_points.why_it_matters: Regulatory scrutiny and safety concerns remain significant hurdles for the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicle technology.

numbers.context: Nvidia's revenue for the last quarter, which beat analyst expectations.
Nvidia's raised growth guidance for the next fiscal year.

summary.lesson: When a company demonstrates consistent financial outperformance, it often signals strong underlying demand that can persist even through leadership changes or geopolitical shifts.
opinions_and_predictions: Kathleen Brooks (XTB) believes Nvidia has a track record of underplaying forecasts and overdelivering on actual results.
Kathleen Brooks (XTB) expects Nvidia to continue pivoting toward high-quality, cash-generating hyperscaler partners.
Kathleen Brooks (XTB) views the board's assertive response to Jensen Huang's statements as a sign of strengthened corporate governance.
Josh Chin (WSJ) notes that most experts do not expect any hard commitments to emerge from the nuclear arms summit.
Josh Chin (WSJ) suggests Beijing values the summit primarily as a symbol of China's arrival as a peer power to the US.
